questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.**

There is a ______ growth of flowers in tropical countries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

__
 
• **Luxuriant:** (of vegetation) rich and profuse in growth; lush.
 
• **Plenty:** a large or sufficient amount or quantity; more than enough.
 
• **Powerful:** having great power or strength.
 
• **Pious:** devoutly religious; (of a hope) sincere but unlikely to be fulfilled.

The sentence talks about the growth of flowers in tropical countries and other options do not match in the context. Hence they are incorrect.

*There is a luxuriant__ growth of flowers in tropical countries.*

questions.question:

A** nursery** is a place where plants and trees are grown for sale or for planting elsewhere.

questions.question:

The old lady nearly __dead from fright.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

**'died of'** means died because of (something.)

 
• Let's see an example:

Thus the correct sentence will be: *The old lady nearly died of fright.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

Sacred
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

 
• **Sacred:** connected with God; dedicated or to consecrated to God or to a religious purpose
 
• **Holy:** dedicated or consecrated to God or a religious purpose; sacred.

 **Holy** is synonymous with **Sacred.**
 
• **Valued:** considered to be important or beneficial; cherished.
 
• **Precious:** of great value; not to be wasted or treated carelessly.
 
• **Scarce:** (especially of food, money, or some other resource) insufficient for the demand.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

 
• **Accurate(adjective):** (especially of information, measurements, or predictions) correct in all details; exact.
 
• **Precise(adjective):** marked by exactness and accuracy of expression or detail.

**Precise** is synonymous with **accurate.**

 
• **Compact(adjective):** closely and neatly packed together; dense.
 
• **Capable(adjective):** having the ability, or quality necessary to do or achieve a specified thing.
 
• **Erroneous(adjective):** wrong; incorrect.

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.**

The minister gave an ______ that strict action would be taken against the culprits.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**assurance**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meaning of the words given in the options are:**

 
 
• ** Assurance(noun):** a positive declaration intended to give confidence; a promise; confidence or certainty in one's own abilities.
 
• **Ambition(noun):** a strong desire to do or achieve something.
 
• **Admission(noun):** a statement acknowledging the truth of something.
 
• **Insurance(noun):** a thing providing protection against a possible eventuality.
 
 
 
• No other option except 'assurance' fits best in the blank.

 

Thus the sentence with the correct option will be: *The minister gave an assurance__ that strict action would be taken against the culprits.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Scarcely had the passengers boarded the plane __when the captain welcomed them__.

options.text: when the captain had welcomed them

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4.**

The **co-relative conjunction *scarcely...when*** is correctly used in the sentence.

It is used as an interrogative sentence with a structure like:

**Helping verb + Subject + main verb**

Scarcely + had + the passengers + boarded the plane when the captain welcomed them.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

*There are numerous__ errors in your assignment.*

questions.question:
**Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.**

To rise in value
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Appreciate:** to rise in value

 
 
• **Example**: Living in the city has taught me to *appreciate* the differences between people.
 
 

Let us look at the meanings of other words:

 
• **Extend:** cause to cover a wider area; make larger.

 
 
• Example: The caves extend for some 15 kilometres.
 
 
 
• **Depreciate:** diminish in value over a period of time.
 
 
• Example: The demand for foreign currency **depreciates **the real value of local currencies
 
 
 
• **Enlarge:** make or become larger or more extensive.
 
 
• Example: As time advanced there was a growing tendency to **enlarge** the royal seal.​
 
 

Hence, option 1 is correct.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

He went to work but returned back immediately.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

The error is in the part **'but returned back'.**

It is **redundant to use 'back' after 'returned'**. The word 'back' is implied by the word 'returned'.

Thus the correct sentence will be: *He went to work but returned immediately.*

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The present what I buy for you yesterday was very expensive.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The error is in the part 'what I buy'.

We see that 'yesterday' expresses the adverb of **time. **Hence simple past tense of the verb **'bought'** must be used.

Also the correct usage of **relative pronoun 'that'** must be used indicating back to 'the present'. 'What' is an incorrect usage.

Thus the correct sentence will be: *The present that I bought for you yesterday was very expensive.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. who.**

We need to use the correct pronoun in the blank. Let us look at the usage of all the mentioned pronouns:

 
• Which is used in asking for information specifying one or more people or things from a definite set.
 
• Whom is used instead of ‘who’ as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• That is used to identify a specific person or thing observed or heard by the speaker.
 
• **Who** is used to introduce a clause giving further information about a person or people previously mentioned.

The most appropriate word is 'who' as it is used to refer to the young boy in the news.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2) i.e. from.**

Let us look at the usage of the prepositions-

 
• At means 'present in a specific location or the time when an event takes place'.
 
• **From** means 'indicating the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts'.
 
• For means 'the time for which an action is performed'.
 
• To means 'indicating the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts'.

The most appropriate word is 'from' as it indicates that he returned from the jungle.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1) i.e. say.**

In the given sentence the father is asking a question to Swami. He is asking him what he has to speak/utter about the particular topic.

The closest word to 'utter something' is **'say'.**

So, option 1 is the most appropriate answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3) i.e. think.**

As the father is asking about Swami's opinion in the previous sentence, he first thinks and then responds. He does not know surely about the topic and he is not giving any suggestions. Hence, the most appropriate word is '**think**'.

So, option 3 is the most appropriate answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. grown up.**

**A grown-up is an adult.** Swami mentions that the boy who had fought a tiger must be very strong and someone who is older than a boy. The required word must mean the same as an adult.

So, option 4 is the most appropriate answer.
